lessons.title: Sign in and find your way around
lessons.summary: Learn the header, department navigation, settings, notifications, and the safe way to sign out.
lessons.outcome: You will sign in, identify your workspace and role, open a department, return home, and sign out safely.
lessons.who: Everyone with a MarketSync login. Your menu will be shorter or longer depending on your product, plan, and job role.
before: Your confirmed MarketSync email address
Your password or registered passkey
Your MFA code if your account has MFA enabled

steps.title: Open the sign-in page
steps.body: Go to your MarketSync site and enter the email address attached to your account. On staging, confirm the address contains marketsync-staging-site.onrender.com before using test data.

steps.title: Complete the required sign-in checks
steps.body: Use your password or registered passkey. If an MFA screen appears, enter the code from the method you enrolled; do not share the code with anyone.

steps.title: Confirm the workspace
steps.body: Read the name and role in the top header. MarketSync platform staff may also see a MarketSync OS / DealerOS switch. Dealership users should see their dealership name.

steps.title: Open a department
steps.body: Use the left navigation on desktop or Menu on mobile. Choose a department such as CRM, Inventory, Accounting, or Service. Only paid and permitted departments are shown.

steps.title: Return to the dashboard
steps.body: Choose Dashboard or Executive to return to the daily overview. Use the gear for Profile & Settings and the bell for notifications.

steps.title: Sign out safely
steps.body: Choose Sign Out in the header when using a shared computer. Closing the tab does not always end the session.

lessons.success: Your header shows the correct person, dealership, and role; every visible menu item opens a page you are allowed to use.
automatic: MarketSync filters navigation by your live product subscription, plan, feature switches, role, and permissions.
Your session is refreshed while you work when Keep me signed in is enabled.
problems: Wrong dashboard or missing pages: confirm you used the email tied to the intended dealership, then sign out and back in.
A page returns to the dashboard: your current plan or role may not include it; ask the dealership owner to review your assignment.
Staging appears slow: Render may be waking the service. Wait up to 60 seconds once, then retry.
lessons.safety: Never share a password, MFA code, recovery code, or passkey prompt. MarketSync support will not ask for them.

lessons.title: Turn on multi-factor authentication (MFA)
lessons.summary: Protect your account with a true second factor and verify that the current session reaches AAL2.
lessons.outcome: You will enroll an authenticator-app factor, verify it, save recovery codes, and confirm MFA is on.
lessons.who: Every user. MFA is required for sensitive actions such as accounting, exports, API keys, integrations, and permission changes.
before: A signed-in MarketSync session
An authenticator app such as 1Password, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or Authy
A safe place to store one-time recovery codes

steps.title: Open Security settings
steps.body: Open the gear, choose Account, and find the clearly labelled Multi-factor authentication (MFA) & account security card.

steps.title: Start enrollment
steps.body: Choose Turn On. If MarketSync says MFA is already enabled, do not create another factor; sign out and complete the MFA challenge during the next sign-in.

steps.title: Scan the QR code
steps.body: In your authenticator app choose Add account, scan QR code, and name the entry MarketSync. If scanning fails, type the displayed secret into the app.

steps.title: Verify the six-digit code
steps.body: Enter the current six-digit number before it expires and choose Turn It On. MarketSync promotes this session immediately so sensitive features work without another enrollment.

steps.title: Save recovery codes
steps.body: Download or copy the one-time backup codes and store them in a password manager or locked physical location. Each code can be used only once.

steps.title: Test the next sign-in
steps.body: Sign out, sign in with your password, and complete the MFA screen. Return to Settings and confirm the status says On.

lessons.success: Settings shows MFA On, a fresh login asks for the second factor, and protected pages no longer display MFA_REQUIRED after verification.
automatic: Supabase records the verified factor and adds aal2 to the verified session JWT.
Enrolling a new verified factor invalidates other sessions as a security precaution.
MarketSync records MFA enrollment and challenge events in the security audit log.
problems: Friendly name already exists: restart enrollment; MarketSync removes only unfinished factors before creating a new one.
Code rejected: wait for the next code and ensure the phone clock is set automatically.
MFA still required after enrollment: refresh once; if it continues, sign out and complete the MFA challenge on the fresh login.
Email OTP and passkey login are not the same as an aal2 second factor. Supabase-supported second factors are authenticator TOTP and configured phone messaging.
lessons.safety: A passkey is a strong passwordless sign-in method, but it must not be falsely represented as Supabase aal2 MFA. Never send recovery codes by email or chat.

lessons.title: Complete the dealership setup
lessons.summary: Add the dealership identity, address, operating details, tax settings, hours, and team contact information.
lessons.outcome: Your dealership profile will contain the operating details MarketSync uses across documents, websites, messages, and reports.
lessons.who: Dealer owners, dealer admins, and general managers with Settings permission.
before: Legal dealership name and public display name
Address, phone, website, timezone, currency, tax rates, and business hours
Logo and brand colours if available

steps.title: Open dealership settings
steps.body: Open the gear, choose Dealership, and confirm the dealership name at the top matches the workspace you intend to edit.

steps.title: Enter identity and contact details
steps.body: Complete the legal name, public name, address, main phone, website, and operational email recipients. Use monitored company addresses.

steps.title: Set regional rules
steps.body: Choose the correct timezone, currency, province or state, and tax configuration. These settings affect appointment times and financial calculations.

steps.title: Add business hours
steps.body: Enter sales and service hours carefully, including closed days. AI booking and public website availability use these values.

steps.title: Add branding
steps.body: Upload a clear logo and choose approved colours. Preview both light and dark text before saving.

steps.title: Save and verify
steps.body: Save each section, reload Settings, and confirm the values remain. Open the dashboard header and a public-facing page to verify the correct dealership identity.

lessons.success: The correct dealership name appears in the header and all saved address, time, currency, tax, and hours fields reload accurately.
automatic: MarketSync reuses approved dealership data in messages, documents, website pages, AI context, and reports.
Changes to protected settings are recorded in the audit system.
problems: Permission denied: confirm your RBAC role includes settings.manage and that you are in the correct dealership.
Times appear wrong: correct the dealership timezone, then reload appointments.
Logo looks blurry: upload a larger PNG with transparent background.
lessons.safety: Tax and legal disclosure settings affect customer documents. Have dealership management review them before real use.

lessons.title: Invite a team member and assign the right role
lessons.summary: Create a dealership login, choose the job role, explain the invitation, and verify the user sees only permitted products.
lessons.outcome: A team member will receive a MarketSync-branded invitation and open the correct role-based dashboard.
lessons.who: Dealer owners, dealer admins, and authorized managers with Users Manage permission.
before: The employee's correct work email and full name
Their department and job responsibilities
The products they should be able to use

steps.title: Open Team settings
steps.body: Open Settings, choose Team, and verify the dealership name before adding anyone.

steps.title: Choose Add or Invite user
steps.body: Enter the employee's full name and work email. Do not reuse an email that belongs to a different person's account.

steps.title: Assign the job role
steps.body: Choose the closest operational role: manager, salesperson, BDC, F&I, service manager, technician, accounting, or read only. Avoid admin unless the person manages access and settings.

steps.title: Assign products if needed
steps.body: Leave product membership empty to inherit all dealership products, or explicitly restrict the person to Facebook, AI Dealer, or DealerOS.

steps.title: Send the invitation
steps.body: Confirm the summary and send. The invitation should be delivered through MarketSync email branding using Resend.

steps.title: Verify first login
steps.body: Ask the employee to open the latest invitation, set credentials, sign in, and confirm their name, dealership, role, and navigation.

lessons.success: The team list shows the user as active and their first login displays the correct dealership, role, products, and department pages.
automatic: MarketSync creates the profile and RBAC role assignment for the same dealership.
The invitation and role assignment are written to security audit records.
Navigation and API permissions are recalculated from live roles and subscriptions.
problems: Invitation link cannot be reached: resend the latest invitation and confirm FRONTEND_URL points to the current site.
Permission denied for user_roles: the backend service role requires the correct table grants; do not work around it with public access.
User sees the wrong plan: check the dealership subscription and product membership, then have the user sign out and back in.
lessons.safety: Use least privilege. Never give accounting, billing, export, API key, or user-management authority solely to make a page visible.

lessons.title: Connect and sync dealership inventory
lessons.summary: Add the dealership inventory source, run a sync, and verify vehicles, photos, prices, stock numbers, and source links.
lessons.outcome: Your inventory source will be connected and a verified set of active vehicles will appear in MarketSync.
lessons.who: Dealer admins and inventory managers with Inventory Edit permission.
before: The dealership inventory page URL or supported feed credentials
A known stock number and VIN to use for verification
Permission to import dealership vehicle data

steps.title: Open Inventory
steps.body: Choose Inventory and locate the Feeds or Inventory source panel. Confirm you are in the correct dealership.

steps.title: Add the source
steps.body: Choose Add source, enter the dealer inventory URL or feed details, and save. Use the public inventory listing, not an admin-only URL.

steps.title: Run the first sync
steps.body: Choose Sync now once. Allow the job to complete; repeatedly clicking can create unnecessary work without speeding it up.

steps.title: Read the sync result
steps.body: Review added, updated, sold or removed, skipped, and failed counts. Open errors before assuming missing stock is an entitlement problem.

steps.title: Verify a real unit
steps.body: Search the known stock number or VIN. Confirm year, make, model, trim, condition, price, mileage, photos, and availability.

steps.title: Verify the dealer listing link
steps.body: Open View Details and confirm it reaches the exact stock page on the dealer's own website through source_url.

lessons.success: The feed shows a successful last run and the known vehicle matches the dealer website, including a working dealer stock-page link.
automatic: MarketSync normalizes source fields and updates matching inventory records.
Vehicles carry their source URL so AI and inventory cards can open the dealer's original listing.
Scheduled syncing uses the configured sync interval after the first successful connection.
problems: Zero vehicles: confirm the source URL is public and the site is not blocking the scraper.
Vehicle missing: search by exact VIN or stock number and inspect the last sync errors.
Old price or photo: run one manual sync and compare the source page timestamp before editing manually.
lessons.safety: Do not connect production dealer credentials to a training dealership. Use schema-safe staging data for recordings.

lessons.title: Add a vehicle manually
lessons.summary: Create a complete inventory record when a feed is unavailable or a vehicle has just arrived.
lessons.outcome: A new vehicle will appear in the correct dealership inventory with enough information for CRM, website, and posting workflows.
lessons.who: Users with Inventory Edit permission, usually inventory managers, sales managers, or dealer admins.
before: VIN and stock number
Year, make, model, trim, condition, price, mileage, and colours
At least one approved vehicle photo if publishing immediately

steps.title: Open Inventory
steps.body: Choose Inventory, then Add vehicle. Confirm the form belongs to the intended dealership.

steps.title: Decode the VIN
steps.body: Enter the 17-character VIN and choose Decode when available. Review every returned field; VIN services can be incomplete.

steps.title: Enter required stock details
steps.body: Complete stock number, condition, status, price, mileage, exterior and interior colours, and acquisition details your dealership tracks.

steps.title: Add photos
steps.body: Upload approved images, place the strongest exterior angle first, and remove duplicates or private information.

steps.title: Add listing content
steps.body: Write or generate a factual description. Verify equipment, warranty, condition, and pricing statements before approval.

steps.title: Save and verify
steps.body: Save once, search the stock number, open the card, and confirm it is available in the correct inventory view.

lessons.success: The vehicle appears once, under the correct dealership, with a unique VIN and stock number and the intended available status.
automatic: MarketSync stamps dealership, creator, and timestamps on the record.
Authorized product pages can reuse the inventory record without retyping vehicle details.
problems: Duplicate VIN or stock number: search existing and sold inventory before creating another record.
Permission warning: confirm inventory.edit rather than changing the user to a broad admin role.
Vehicle does not appear on Facebook or website: saving inventory does not automatically mean the destination is enabled or published.
lessons.safety: Do not invent decoded options or accident history. Verify customer-owned trade data before publishing it as dealership inventory.

lessons.title: Post the first vehicle to Facebook Marketplace
lessons.summary: Prepare one complete listing, open the Chrome extension, and post safely without duplicates.
lessons.outcome: One eligible MarketSync vehicle will be posted to the correct Facebook Marketplace account.
lessons.who: Facebook Solo users and dealership sales representatives assigned to Facebook inventory.
before: Chrome with the MarketSync extension installed and pinned
A signed-in Facebook account allowed to use Marketplace
A MarketSync vehicle with required details and photos

steps.title: Choose eligible inventory
steps.body: Open Facebook Inventory and select an available vehicle that has a price, mileage, location, description, and clear photos.

steps.title: Check posting safety
steps.body: Review Safe to post, rest-period, daily-limit, and duplicate indicators. Do not force a post during a required rest period.

steps.title: Open the extension
steps.body: Choose Post to Facebook. If Chrome asks for site access, allow only the permissions described by MarketSync.

steps.title: Review the prepared listing
steps.body: Verify category, year, make, model, price, mileage, condition, location, description, and photo order before submission.

steps.title: Complete Facebook fields
steps.body: Let the extension fill supported fields, then complete any Facebook-required fields that remain. Do not navigate away while the posting step is active.

steps.title: Publish and record the result
steps.body: Publish once, return to MarketSync, and confirm the listing status and timestamp. Open Facebook to verify the live result.

lessons.success: The vehicle has one live Facebook listing, MarketSync records the post, and the Facebook-focused leaderboard reflects eligible activity.
automatic: MarketSync prepares listing text and images from the approved vehicle record.
Posting events feed the Facebook posting leaderboard and safety limits.
problems: Extension times out: keep the Marketplace tab open, refresh the extension, and resume from the same vehicle rather than starting a duplicate.
Wrong Facebook account: sign out of the unintended Facebook profile before posting.
Leaderboard missing: confirm the account includes fb.leaderboard and the post was recorded successfully.
lessons.safety: Follow Facebook rules and dealership advertising law. Never post customer information, misleading prices, or unapproved claims.

lessons.title: Reply as a human in an AI conversation
lessons.summary: Open an AI lead conversation, understand its context, reply personally, and return control safely.
lessons.outcome: You will take over one conversation, send an accurate reply, and leave a clear handoff state.
lessons.who: AI Dealer users with access to dealership conversations and leads.
before: An AI Dealer conversation in the inbox
The dealership's approved pricing, booking, and escalation rules
Permission to contact the customer

steps.title: Open AI Conversations
steps.body: Choose AI Dealer, then Conversations. Filter by unread, needs human, lead status, or customer name.

steps.title: Read the full context
steps.body: Review the transcript, customer details, requested vehicle, source page, AI summary, and any appointment or lead already created.

steps.title: Take control
steps.body: Choose Reply as human or Take over before typing. This prevents the AI from replying over top of you.

steps.title: Write a factual response
steps.body: Answer the customer's question directly. Verify live price, availability, stock number, and links before sending.

steps.title: Send and classify
steps.body: Send once, then assign or update the lead status if the conversation requires sales follow-up.

steps.title: Return control deliberately
steps.body: Leave the conversation in human mode if a person owns the next step. Return to AI only when the automation is allowed to continue.

lessons.success: The message appears in the conversation with a human sender indicator and the customer/lead ownership state matches the next action.
automatic: MarketSync records the reply in the conversation timeline.
Vehicle cards prefer the dealer's source_url so the customer reaches the real stock page.
Lead and appointment actions remain tied to the same dealership and conversation.
problems: Conversation page shows unrelated modules: confirm the account is assigned to the AI Dealer product and not a DealerOS fallback.
No vehicle image or price: inspect the inventory source record and last sync.
Customer received no reply: verify the configured channel and delivery status before sending again.
lessons.safety: Do not promise availability, approval, payment, or trade value without verification. Respect SMS, email, and marketing consent.

lessons.title: Create a customer appointment
lessons.summary: Schedule an appointment from a customer record with the right owner, time, purpose, and reminders.
lessons.outcome: A dated appointment will appear on the customer timeline and the correct user's calendar view.
lessons.who: Sales, BDC, managers, and authorized service users who can view the customer.
before: A customer record with a confirmed contact method
Agreed date, time, purpose, and assigned person
The dealership timezone and hours configured correctly

steps.title: Open the customer
steps.body: Search CRM and open the exact customer. Check for duplicates before scheduling.

steps.title: Choose Add appointment
steps.body: Select the appointment action from the customer record rather than creating an unlinked calendar entry.

steps.title: Enter the appointment
steps.body: Choose type, date, start time, expected duration, assigned person, and concise notes about the customer's goal.

steps.title: Confirm communication
steps.body: Choose only reminder channels the customer has consented to receive and confirm the displayed phone or email.

steps.title: Save and verify
steps.body: Save, then confirm the appointment appears on the customer timeline and Appointments page under the correct date and owner.

lessons.success: The appointment appears once on both the customer timeline and calendar with the correct local time and assignment.
automatic: MarketSync ties the appointment to the dealership, customer, and assigned user.
Configured reminders and connected calendars can receive the appointment.
problems: Time is shifted: correct the dealership timezone before rescheduling.
Appointment is missing from a rep's view: confirm assignment and the rep's product/role membership.
Duplicate reminders: check for duplicate appointments and connected-calendar rules.
lessons.safety: Record only operational notes needed for the appointment. Do not place credit or sensitive identity data in appointment notes.

lessons.title: Respond to and assign a new lead
lessons.summary: Acknowledge a lead quickly, verify its source and customer, assign ownership, and record the next action.
lessons.outcome: A new lead will have a verified owner, response, status, and scheduled next step.
lessons.who: Salespeople, BDC, sales managers, and dealer admins with lead access.
before: A new lead in the queue
Current inventory availability and dealer response standards
Customer communication consent and preferred channel

steps.title: Open the new-lead queue
steps.body: Choose CRM, then Leads, and sort by newest or response-time warning.

steps.title: Verify the record
steps.body: Read source, customer contact information, message, vehicle, existing customer matches, and any AI response before acting.

steps.title: Acknowledge the lead
steps.body: Open the lead and mark it acknowledged so the team knows it is being handled.

steps.title: Assign the owner
steps.body: Choose the correct salesperson or BDC owner according to routing rules. Managers can transfer when required.

steps.title: Send the first response
steps.body: Answer the stated question, confirm only verified information, and invite the next useful action such as an appointment.

steps.title: Create the follow-up
steps.body: Set lead status and add a dated task or appointment so the lead cannot disappear after the first message.

lessons.success: The lead shows an owner, first response time, current status, and a visible next task or appointment.
automatic: MarketSync records lead source, assignment, response time, communications, and timeline events.
Routing and AI automation may create or update tasks according to dealership configuration.
problems: Cannot assign: the manager needs lead.assign; a salesperson may only work their assigned records.
Duplicate customer: merge or link according to dealership process rather than creating a second person.
ADF delivery failed: inspect integration delivery status and retry once after correcting configuration.
lessons.safety: Respect consent and dealership contact hours. Never expose another customer's data or send unverified financing claims.

lessons.title: Complete the daily accounting check without being an accountant
lessons.summary: Use the daily briefing to confirm yesterday's money moved into the right buckets and flag anything that needs professional review.
lessons.outcome: You will review the daily accounting summary, match operational events to money movements, and create a clean exception list.
lessons.who: Dealer owners, managers, and accounting users. You do not need bookkeeping knowledge to perform this review; approval and corrections still require the appropriate authority.
before: Yesterday's delivered deals, deposits, expenses, refunds, service closes, and bank activity
The dealership's accounting tolerance and current period
MFA completed for the current session

steps.title: Open Accounting
steps.body: Choose Accounting and read the date, dealership, period, and status at the top. Stop if the wrong dealership or period is shown.

steps.title: Read the summary in business language
steps.body: Compare cash in, cash out, sales, cost, expenses, receivables, and payables to what the dealership actually did. A number is a clue, not proof by itself.

steps.title: Review operational events
steps.body: Open delivered deals, deposits, approved expenses, service closes, commissions, and refunds. Check that each expected event exists once.

steps.title: Review exceptions
steps.body: Open unmatched, failed, duplicate, out-of-balance, or missing-reference items. Assign an owner and add a plain note describing what is known.

steps.title: Check bank matching
steps.body: Compare imported bank transactions to recorded activity. Match only when date, amount, party, and purpose support the match.

steps.title: Finish the daily review
steps.body: Confirm resolved items, leave uncertain items open, and record who must investigate. Do not change an entry merely to make the warning disappear.

lessons.success: Every known daily money event is either matched and explained or remains on a short assigned exception list with a next action.
automatic: MarketSync creates accounting events from supported dealership operations.
Rules can draft journal treatment, but protected changes and period actions remain permission- and MFA-controlled.
Exceptions and changes retain an audit trail.
problems: MFA required after verification: refresh the session or sign out and complete the MFA challenge; do not disable MFA to bypass the control.
A total is different from the bank: find timing differences, duplicates, fees, refunds, or missing events before adjusting anything.
Permission denied: accounting.view is required to read and accounting.edit is required to change protected records.
lessons.safety: Never guess a tax, account, lender, or amount. Leave uncertain items open and ask the controller or accountant. MarketSync supports the workflow; it does not replace professional judgment.

lessons.title: Upload, approve, and reimburse an expense
lessons.summary: Capture a receipt, explain the business purpose, route approval, and verify payment without losing the source document.
lessons.outcome: A documented dealership expense will move from draft to approved and reimbursed with a complete audit trail.
lessons.who: Accounting users and authorized managers with Accounting Edit permission and completed MFA.
before: Readable receipt or invoice
Vendor, date, amount, tax, business purpose, department, and payment method
The correct approval authority

steps.title: Open Expenses
steps.body: Choose Accounting, then Expenses, and select Add expense.

steps.title: Upload the document
steps.body: Attach the receipt or invoice. If receipt scanning fills fields, compare every field to the original before saving.

steps.title: Explain the transaction
steps.body: Enter vendor, date, subtotal, taxes, total, department, business purpose, payment method, and reimbursable person when applicable.

steps.title: Save as draft
steps.body: Save the draft and verify the attachment opens. Correct missing or inaccurate details before approval.

steps.title: Approve with authority
steps.body: The authorized approver reviews the source document and chooses Approve. A person should not approve their own expense when dealership policy forbids it.

steps.title: Record payment or reimbursement
steps.body: After money moves, record payment date, method, and reference. Verify the status and related bank match.

lessons.success: The expense total matches the source document, shows approval and payment states, retains the attachment, and identifies every person who changed it.
automatic: MarketSync timestamps creation, approval, and payment actions.
Authorized expense events can feed accounting entries and reconciliation.
problems: Receipt scan is wrong: edit the draft to match the original; never approve OCR without review.
Cannot approve: complete MFA and confirm accounting.edit plus dealership approval policy.
Duplicate expense: search vendor, date, and amount before uploading again.
lessons.safety: Mask unrelated personal information. Preserve the original tax document and follow dealership approval and retention rules.

lessons.title: Reconcile a bank account and fix a variance
lessons.summary: Match bank activity to MarketSync records, explain timing differences, and resolve variances without forcing the books to balance.
lessons.outcome: A reconciliation period will have supported matches, a verified ending balance, and no unexplained difference.
lessons.who: Accounting users and authorized managers with Accounting Edit permission and completed MFA.
before: Official bank statement opening and closing balances
Imported or entered bank transactions for the same date range
Access to deposits, expenses, refunds, and deal records

steps.title: Start the correct period
steps.body: Open Accounting, then Reconciliation. Choose the account and exact statement start/end dates.

steps.title: Enter statement balances
steps.body: Type the official opening and closing balances exactly. Confirm currency and account before continuing.

steps.title: Match clear transactions
steps.body: Match items only when amount, date, party, and purpose support the relationship. One bank deposit may match a documented batch.

steps.title: Classify legitimate differences
steps.body: Identify outstanding cheques, deposits in transit, bank fees, interest, refunds, duplicates, and missing records. Attach evidence or a note.

steps.title: Correct the source, not the symptom
steps.body: If a dealership record is wrong, correct it through the authorized source workflow. Do not create an unexplained adjustment merely to reach zero.

steps.title: Review and close
steps.body: When the difference is zero and every adjustment is supported, have the authorized reviewer approve and close the reconciliation.

lessons.success: The reconciliation difference is exactly zero for explainable reasons, and every match or adjustment can be traced to a source record.
automatic: MarketSync calculates cleared totals and the remaining variance as matches change.
Closing and correction actions are audited and protected by role and MFA.
problems: Difference equals one transaction: search that exact amount for an unmatched, duplicate, reversed, or wrong-period item.
Opening balance is wrong: verify the previous statement and previous closed reconciliation before changing entries.
Still not zero: leave it open and escalate with the statement, variance, and exception list.
lessons.safety: Do not close an unexplained reconciliation. Period close and financial adjustments may require the controller or external accountant.

lessons.title: Read a profit and loss report in plain language
lessons.summary: Understand revenue, gross profit, expenses, and net income without memorizing accounting jargon.
lessons.outcome: You will explain what the dealership earned, what it spent, and which department or category caused the largest change.
lessons.who: Dealer owners, managers, and accounting users with Accounting View permission and completed MFA.
before: A selected dealership and reporting date range
Awareness of major deliveries, expenses, refunds, and period timing
The comparison period you want to use

steps.title: Open the income statement
steps.body: Choose Accounting, Reports, then Income Statement or Profit & Loss. Confirm dealership, currency, and date range.

steps.title: Read revenue
steps.body: Revenue is what the dealership earned before the costs shown below it. Compare the total to delivered and posted activity for the same period.

steps.title: Read gross profit
steps.body: Gross profit is revenue minus the direct cost of what was sold. Review vehicle, F&I, service, parts, or other departments separately when available.

steps.title: Read operating expenses
steps.body: Expenses are the costs of running the dealership, such as advertising, payroll-related costs, rent, software, and supplies.

steps.title: Read net income
steps.body: Net income is what remains after the report's included expenses. It is not the same as cash in the bank.

steps.title: Investigate, do not edit the report
steps.body: Drill into unusual categories, compare periods, and trace totals to source records. Correct source transactions through their approved workflows.

lessons.success: You can explain the period's revenue, gross profit, operating expenses, and net result and name the records behind any unusual change.
automatic: MarketSync groups posted accounting entries into report categories and calculates totals.
Date and department filters recalculate the report without changing source records.
problems: Profit looks high but cash is low: timing, receivables, payables, debt, inventory, and deposits can differ from reported profit.
A department is empty: confirm its operational events were posted to accounting in the selected period.
Numbers changed after close: inspect audit and change history immediately.
lessons.safety: Use the report for operational understanding, not tax filing or lender certification without accountant review.

lessons.title: Work the MarketSync customer pipeline and create a follow-up
lessons.summary: Move a MarketSync prospect through the SaaS pipeline and make sure the next contact cannot be missed.
lessons.outcome: A MarketSync prospect or customer will have the correct stage, owner, priority, notes, and dated follow-up.
lessons.who: MarketSync platform owners and authorized MarketSync staff. Dealership users do not see this internal course.
before: A real or training prospect in MarketSync OS
The latest call, email, demo, trial, billing, or support context
A clear owner and next action

steps.title: Switch to MarketSync OS
steps.body: Use the workspace switch and confirm the purple MarketSync identity before editing a SaaS customer.

steps.title: Open Customer Pipeline
steps.body: Find the account by dealership, contact, email, or stage. Confirm you are not looking at the DealerOS CRM copy.

steps.title: Update stage and health
steps.body: Choose the stage that reflects reality, record priority or churn risk, and avoid moving a customer solely to improve funnel numbers.

steps.title: Record the interaction
steps.body: Add a concise note describing what happened, the customer's stated need, any commitment, and who owns the next step.

steps.title: Create the follow-up
steps.body: Set a dated task with owner, channel, reason, and expected outcome. Use a real due date rather than an open-ended note.

steps.title: Verify the queue
steps.body: Open Follow-ups and confirm the item appears under the correct owner and date. Complete or reschedule only after the action occurs.

lessons.success: The customer stage matches reality and the MarketSync follow-up queue shows one owned, dated next action.
automatic: MarketSync recalculates funnel and follow-up views from customer stage and task data.
